# Independent audit of selected circuits and localized convex potentials

Audited source:
`candidate b1ef83513bdb0bcf`,
Sections 1--4. The mathematical arguments PASS with the regularity
precision below. No general selected-circuit efficiency bound is proved.

The source author has now applied both requested precision changes to the
main source and strengthened the older interval dependency consistently.
Thus there is no pending repair in this audit.

## Required meaning of regularity at a possible boundary source

For the strict-contact argument, regularity is understood to mean that
the cap-mass map is differentiable in the full hyperplane parameters
(A,b), with its usual coarea first variation. This is stronger than merely
asserting differentiability while the cap is constrained through its
original source Y. The older product-interval dependency phrases its
definition in the latter way; there the own cut is proper before reuse,
so this distinction does not cause a gap. The new boundary-source
extension should state the full-parameter meaning explicitly.

Under that meaning, if a regular critical cap through Y has total
coarea S>0, every different deepest point Y' is strictly outside it.
Interior Y' is excluded by increasing the threshold. If Y' lies on the
same boundary, stationarity of all normals through Y gives zero first
section moment about Y. The cap mass of normals through Y' therefore
has derivative S deltaA dot(Y-Y'). With deltaA=Y'-Y this is
-S||Y'-Y||^2<0. The only required positive section mass is somewhere in
the finite family, not necessarily in the original source fiber.

## Orbit and source arguments

The inverse maps of a finite group form the same group, so the zero
average linear map implies zero average inverse transpose on normals.
Its elements have absolute determinant one. The affine maps on a common
affine centroid graph preserve the actual mixed lattice, all fibers,
the mixed measure, and every ambient halfspace. Averaging an orbit of a
deepest source stays in its actual convex fiber and remains deepest by
quasiconcavity of halfspace depth. The strict-contact fact and positive
continuous normal balance then exclude a second deepest point in that
fiber. Spanning of the normals is not needed: each distinct point would
have to satisfy every strict negative inequality, contradicting balance.

The cap orbit in the centroid shear has one common integer coefficient.
A vertex maximizing that coefficient over the finite integer base has
the required nonnegative offset in every selected cap. One can expose
that single vertex even when the maximizing face is larger. Finite
localization of the potential follows from bounded fibers and the
strictly negative exposing values at every other base.

The radial boundary integrand is nonnegative because each actual fiber
centroid is interior. Its total integral is exactly d times the exposed
fiber volume. Each actual cap trace contains its parallel through-centroid
trace, whose internal cut-plane radial flux vanishes. Therefore its
boundary contribution is at least d times that central cap volume. This
is a valid inclusion argument for oblique caps and does not confuse an
offset cap volume with its radial boundary flux. Proper central traces
carry no boundary surface mass on the cut; the d=1 endpoint case also
satisfies the same identity.

For a standalone definition, eta should explicitly be the sum of fiber
surface measures lifted to the outward-unit-normal bundle (the normal
is defined almost everywhere). This is the meaning in the cited product
dependency and in the audited calculation.

## Response weights and finite optimization

With S_j equal to the total coarea divided by ||u_j|| and b_j=S_j u_j,
the vector b_j is invariant under positive rescaling of a cap equation.
The correspondence rho_j=theta_j S_j is exactly the response-weight
normalization: geometric balance sum rho_j u_j=0 is equivalent to
sum theta_j b_j=0. All S_j are required positive in this correspondence.

The response polytope is compact when nonempty. Any extreme point has
at most rank{(1,b_j)}<=d+1 positive entries by a supported signed linear
dependence. Supremum over potentials commutes with the finite maximum
over these vertices; no potential attainment is inferred. The stated
ordinary LP dual has the correct sign and remains valid in a
rank-deficient span. No minimax exchange is used.

Finally, summing separately normalized nonnegative potentials gives
exact denominator s and preserves each selected individual numerator
from its own summand. The source correctly retains the existence
quantifier for a chosen circuit, the strict-gap epsilon choice, and the
unproved global regularity/variational interfaces. Counterexamples to
every prescribed circuit do not negate this selected-circuit statement.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
